independence_attestation: No betting odds, prediction-market prices or forecast-aggregator numbers were fetched or consulted for this dossier. One analytics-model title probability that surfaced incidentally in a search snippet was deliberately ignored and informed no number. All probabilities derive solely from official/Wikipedia standings and results, dated form/injury/fixture news, Champions League schedule load, and the Premier League's own historical base-rate article; reference classes were set before adjusting on evidence.

base_rate_used.reference_class: elite PL club sitting 2nd-3rd, ~6 pts behind the leader after ~12 games
base_rate_used.source: Premier League historical base-rate article 4475268 (7 champions came from 6+ pts behind after 12 games, several of them Man City)

evidence: After MW11 (table as of 22 Nov 2026): Man City 22 pts, 3rd, GD +8, 6 pts behind Arsenal but level on points with 2nd-placed Brighton
Three league defeats already incl. 3-1 at Nott'm Forest (7 Nov) and a 1-1 draw with Fulham (21 Nov) - visible inconsistency
Haaland in strong scoring form (~12 league goals); Champions League load (Napoli 24 Nov); face Arsenal away 29 Nov

key_sources.title: How many teams have won the title from six points behind after 12 matches

questions.reasoning_summary: Base rate 0.18 (elite club ~6 pts back after 12 games; 7 such champions exist historically, several of them City). Upward adjustment for squad quality and the best comeback pedigree in PL history (+); downward adjustment for three league defeats already and visible early-season inconsistency (losing at Forest, drawing Fulham) plus UCL congestion (-). Net lands at 0.17, a touch below the base rate - the inconsistency outweighs the pedigree with 27 games still to play.
questions.strongest_opposing_case: City have the best comeback pedigree in PL history and 6 pts over 27 games is eminently recoverable; the Nov 29 Arsenal-away fixture is a swing game that could halve the gap - argues for 0.22-0.25.

base_rate_used.reference_class: PL leader by >=6 pts after ~12 games
base_rate_used.source: Premier League article 4475268 (raw 6/6 = 1.00 for 6+ pt leaders after 12 games, regressed heavily for the tiny n=6 sample and for this being after 11 not 12 games)

evidence: Arsenal 28 pts after 11, lead by 6; only two dropped-points games all season (2-2 at Newcastle 21 Nov; a Sept loss at Brighton); best defence
Injuries: Saka (quad, ~4 weeks), Zubimendi (hamstring), Raya (shoulder doubt), Konsa; Saliba returning
Deep unbeaten UCL run = congestion; punishing Nov-Dec run: Dortmund (24 Nov), Man City home (29 Nov), Spurs, Real Madrid (9 Dec)

key_sources.title: Arteta injuries update ahead of Newcastle
How many teams have won the title from six points behind after 12 matches

questions.reasoning_summary: Base rate 0.65 (6+ pt leaders after 12 games are 6/6 historically, but n=6 is tiny and this is after 11 not 12 games, so the raw 100% is regressed heavily). Downward adjustments: two capable chasers tied on 22 rather than one; a cluster of injuries (Saka, Zubimendi, Raya) during the hardest fixture stretch (City, Spurs, Real Madrid) plus UCL load. One mild upward pull from the league-best defence and only two dropped-points games all season. Net 0.60 - still the clear favourite but well short of a lock.
questions.strongest_opposing_case: 27 games (71% of the season) remain; two capable chasers are tied on 22, not one; key injuries during the hardest fixture stretch could erase the cushion - pulls toward ~0.55.

base_rate_used.reference_class: combined share of the current leader + strongest-pedigree chaser (mutually exclusive outcomes)
base_rate_used.source: sum of the Arsenal and Man City components

evidence: Arsenal (0.60) and Man City (0.17) are the two highest-probability clubs; their sum is 0.77
The two remaining credible contenders (Brighton on GD, Liverpool on pedigree) cap this below ~0.80
questions.reasoning_summary: This is the disjunction of two mutually exclusive outcomes, so the probability is the sum of the Arsenal (0.60) and Man City (0.17) components = 0.77. It is coherent by construction (>= each individual component). The remaining ~0.23 is held by Brighton (best GD in the league), a recovering Liverpool, and the long-shot field, which keeps this comfortably below certainty despite the two named clubs being the strongest in the race.
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Brighton (best GD in the league) and a recovering Liverpool jointly hold meaningful probability, so this should not approach certainty.

base_rate_used.reference_class: elite PL club ~7 pts behind, 4th after ~12 games
base_rate_used.source: Premier League article 4475268 comeback precedents (recent champions have come from behind)

evidence: Liverpool 21 pts, 4th, 7 behind Arsenal (a larger gap than City's 6)
Form recovering: beat Crystal Palace 3-1 (8 Nov); Isak scoring (~7 league goals); but lost 1-0 head-to-head to Arsenal (1 Nov)
questions.reasoning_summary: Base rate 0.12 (elite club ~7 pts back, 4th after 12 games; recent champions have occasionally come from behind). Downward adjustment because Liverpool's 7-point gap is the largest of the three main chasers and they already lost the head-to-head to Arsenal (-); a mild upward pull from recovering form (3-1 at Palace) and Isak's scoring (+). Net 0.10, marginally below the base rate given the gap is wider than City's.
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Defending-champion-calibre squads routinely close 7-point gaps; if the recovery is real Liverpool could be nearer 0.15.

base_rate_used.reference_class: champion emerges from the clubs at/near the top of the table after ~12 games
base_rate_used.source: historical dominance of top-of-table clubs; the PL title is always won from the leading pack

evidence: Component sum for the frozen set {Arsenal, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Chelsea}: Arsenal 0.60 + Man City 0.17 + Liverpool 0.10 + Brighton 0.06 + Chelsea 0.02 = 0.95
Brighton kept modest (best GD but no title pedigree, just lost 2-0 at home to Hull, players downplaying a title bid); Chelsea minimal (8th, 12 pts back)

key_sources.title: Brighton rise to second but Gross insists Seagulls aren't in the title race

questions.reasoning_summary: Base rate 0.92 (the champion almost always emerges from the leading pack after 12 games). Built up from the component probabilities of the five frozen clubs: Arsenal 0.60 + Man City 0.17 + Liverpool 0.10 + Brighton 0.06 + Chelsea 0.02 = 0.95, which lands just above the base rate. The ~0.05 remainder is deliberately left for a dark horse outside the set (Bournemouth, Leeds, Everton, Spurs, Villa, Newcastle) given 27 games remain; the figure satisfies coherence (>= Arsenal+City+Liverpool = 0.87).
questions.strongest_opposing_case: 27 games remain; a side outside the frozen set (Bournemouth, Leeds, Everton, Spurs, Villa, Newcastle) could surge - justifies leaving ~5% for the field.
